svg.title: States off the ladder: Integral Psychology (2000) beside Integral Spirituality (2006)
svg.desc: Left: a single ladder of ten rungs from Integral Psychology, archaic, magic, mythic, rational, pluralistic, integral, and then psychic, subtle, causal, nondual on top, the top four marked as states. Right: the Wilber-Combs lattice from Integral Spirituality, the six structure-stages up the side and the four states, gross or psychic, subtle, causal, nondual, across the top, twenty-four cells. The four top rungs of the ladder have become the column headers; the six lower rungs have become the row labels. Below, a verbatim passage from Integral Spirituality chapter 4 and a note that Integral Psychology already said states are available at any stage.
svg.text: WILBER WIKI · WHAT CHANGED BETWEEN TWO BOOKS
In 2000 the mystical states sit on top of one developmental ladder. In 2006 the same words name a second axis.

rect.title: integral × gross/psychic: a gross-state experience, interpreted through the integral stage
integral × subtle: a subtle-state experience, interpreted through the integral stage
integral × causal: a causal-state experience, interpreted through the integral stage
integral × nondual: a nondual-state experience, interpreted through the integral stage
pluralistic × gross/psychic: a gross-state experience, interpreted through the pluralistic stage
pluralistic × subtle: a subtle-state experience, interpreted through the pluralistic stage
pluralistic × causal: a causal-state experience, interpreted through the pluralistic stage
pluralistic × nondual: a nondual-state experience, interpreted through the pluralistic stage

rational × subtle: a subtle-state experience, interpreted through the rational stage
rational × causal: a causal-state experience, interpreted through the rational stage
rational × nondual: a nondual-state experience, interpreted through the rational stage

mythic × subtle: a subtle-state experience, interpreted through the mythic stage
mythic × causal: a causal-state experience, interpreted through the mythic stage
mythic × nondual: a nondual-state experience, interpreted through the mythic stage
magic × gross/psychic: a gross-state experience, interpreted through the magic stage
magic × subtle: a subtle-state experience, interpreted through the magic stage
magic × causal: a causal-state experience, interpreted through the magic stage
magic × nondual: a nondual-state experience, interpreted through the magic stage
archaic × gross/psychic: a gross-state experience, interpreted through the archaic stage
archaic × subtle: a subtle-state experience, interpreted through the archaic stage
archaic × causal: a causal-state experience, interpreted through the archaic stage
archaic × nondual: a nondual-state experience, interpreted through the archaic stage

svg.text: each cell: a state experience, interpreted through a stage · 6 × 4 here; Wilber counts 7 × 4 = 28

g.text: “…gross/psychic, subtle, causal, and nondual were no longer stages stacked on top of the
Western conventional stages, but were states (including altered states and peak
experiences) that can and did occur alongside any of those stages.”
◇ What changed is the picture, and the weight put on it: Integral Psychology (2000)
already says these states are “available to human beings at virtually any stage of
growth” (ch. 1) and traces the grid idea to A Sociable God (1983). The row names
are IS's Gebser-like list; the small labels give the nearest IP chart-1 worldview.
Sources: Integral Psychology, chart 1 (structure spine, worldview column) · Integral Spirituality, ch. 4 · redrawn for wilber.wiki; not a reproduction of a published figure
